title: SpaceX seeks $40 billion financing led by Apollo to buy Nvidia chips, FT reports
key_facts: The Financial Times reported SpaceX is seeking to raise $40 billion, led by Apollo Global, to buy Nvidia chips, citing people familiar with the matter.
About $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt; Apollo expected to lead and help market the debt.
Pimco was among a small group of lenders in talks to fund the deal.
Musk earlier said SpaceX would exclusively use Nvidia chips in its Colossus data centers.
SpaceX folded in Musk's xAI before its IPO earlier this year and powers its Grok AI through Colossus.
SpaceX signed deals to rent out Colossus computing capacity to other AI developers, chiefly Anthropic and Google.
quote_evidence: Elon Musk's rocket and artificial intelligence firm is seeking to raise about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt for the order, with Apollo expected to lead the deal and help market the debt, the FT report said.
The planned fundraise highlights the large sums that are being poured into data centers, chips, and other infrastructure needed to run AI.
why_it_matters_hint: Large debt raise to buy Nvidia chips shows the scale of AI infrastructure spending.
